content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am looking for the best method to create a historical trend for analog data in [product_name]. At the moment, I use the [product_name] web editor trend tool, but it doesn't allow for historical trends. I am considering logging the data into an SQL database and developing my own trending application. However, I'm interested to know if any ready-made solutions exist for this purpose. Thank you in advance.

Hi, Currently, an online trend view is not available with [product_name]. The main reason appears to be limited memory within [product_name]. However, there are some alternatives: 1. You can use the datalog feature in [product_name], which utilizes its internal memory. This is limited to about 200 records. To access this data, you need to switch the device to STOP mode before uploading. If you need more records, you can connect a standard memory card, and [product_name] will then record and store data on it. 2. Another option is to use a separate HMI device, provided it supports trend view functions. 3. Alternatively, devices like IoT platforms, Raspberry Pi, Arduino, etc. can record and display data via S7 or Modbus communication. Hope this helps.
If you're looking for an off-the-shelf solution, consider an HMI panel.

[product_name] can write log data to a memory card, but only a short trend period is displayed in the web editor. It should be possible to download or view log data using a button in newer versions of the web editor. Users would benefit from both live and historical data views—covering durations like a week, month, or year—depending on user-defined trend settings in enhanced versions of the web editor. If current hardware is insufficient, I hope future versions of [product_name] will support trend logging for up to one year using a memory card, potentially distributed across multiple log files. Similar to camera DVRs or car cams, the data could be recorded in a loop, overwriting older files once the memory card is full.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report limitations in the [product_name] web editor’s trend functionality, specifically lacking support for historical trend visualization and restricted trend durations due to hardware constraints. The existing solution only enables short-term data viewing and requires manual steps, like switching the hardware to STOP mode to retrieve recorded data. The memory limit and absence of built-in options for long-term historical analysis are causing frustration, emphasizing a need for enhanced capabilities for extended data logging and trend review.
analysis.user_expectations: Users would like intuitive built-in support for historical analog data trend visualization and logging, ideally with the ability to review and retrieve data spanning up to one year.
